P2329: Blessed is the one who sent his servant a standard of right and wrong to warn all peoples; he rules heavens and earth, has no child or partner, and measured all he created. Yet people adopt gods that create nothing, are themselves created, and control neither harm, benefit, death, life nor resurrection. Deniers call it a lie others helped invent.
P1721: These are verses of a clear scripture. Deniers may one day wish they had submitted; leave them to eat, enjoy and be lulled by hope. No town perished except at its fixed term. They call the recipient of the reminder mad and demand angels; angels come only with final truth, leaving no respite. God sent the reminder and guards it.
P7922: God, the only god, living and sustaining, sent this scripture confirming earlier ones he had sent as guidance. Deniers face severe punishment. Nothing is hidden from him; he shapes people in the womb. Some verses are clear and foundational, others ambiguous; the crooked-hearted chase the ambiguous to stir discord, while those firm in knowledge say they believe it all.
P6586: People are told to fear their Lord, for the quaking of the final hour is terrible: nursing mothers will forget their infants, pregnant women miscarry, and people will seem drunk though they are not. Yet some argue about God without knowledge and follow every rebellious devil, who is fated to mislead his followers into the punishment of fire.
P5125: This scripture comes from God, mighty and knowing, who forgives sin, accepts repentance, punishes severely and gives abundantly. Only deniers dispute his signs; do not be fooled by their free movement through the land. Earlier peoples also denied, plotted to seize their messengers and argued with falsehood against truth, and were seized. So deniers are destined for fire.
P4699: Everything in heaven and earth glorifies God. Believers are rebuked for saying what they do not do, which God hates; he loves those who fight for him in ranks like a solid wall. One prophet asked his people why they hurt him; another confirmed earlier law and foretold a named messenger after him, but was called a sorcerer.
P6972: In the name of the merciful God: praise belongs to him, lord of all worlds, compassionate, master of the day of judgment. The speakers declare that they worship him alone and seek help from him alone, and ask to be guided on the straight path of those he has favored, not of those under anger or those gone astray.
P4522: By the bright morning and the still night, the listener is assured his Lord has neither abandoned nor disliked him; what comes later will be better, and he will be satisfied. He was found orphaned and sheltered, lost and guided, poor and enriched. So he must not oppress orphans or repel beggars, and should proclaim his Lord's favor.
P7947: God reveals to the listener as to those before him. The heavens nearly split while angels praise him and seek forgiveness for earth's inhabitants. God, not the listener, watches those who take other protectors. His recitation, in a named language, warns the chief city and its surroundings of the gathering day: some to the garden, some to the blaze.
P8010: An account of God's mercy to a servant who prayed in secret: his bones are weak, his hair has turned white, yet his prayers have never gone unanswered. Fearing what his relatives will do after him, and with a barren wife, he asks for an heir pleasing to God. He is promised a son with a name never given before.
P9903: When the sky splits, stars scatter, seas burst and graves are overturned, each soul will know what it did and neglected. Man is asked what deceived him about the generous Lord who shaped and proportioned him. People deny the judgment, yet noble scribes record their deeds. The righteous will be in bliss, the wicked in fire on judgment day.
P6106: Everything glorifies God, the holy and wise king. He raised among an unlettered people a messenger from themselves to recite his signs, purify them and teach scripture and wisdom, though they had been in error, and for others yet to join them. Those given an earlier law who failed to carry it are like a donkey loaded with books.
P1650: God voids deeds of those who deny and obstruct his way, but forgives and sets right those who believe what his messenger received. In battle believers strike necks, then bind captives, later freeing them by grace or ransom, until war ends. God could punish deniers himself but tests people by one another; the slain's deeds are not lost.
P8036: Everything glorifies God. He drove deniers among the scripture-holders from their homes, though no one expected them to leave and they trusted their fortresses. God came from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts; they tore down their houses alongside the believers. Had exile not been decreed, they would have been punished here; fire awaits them.
P5492: The listener is asked whether he has not seen how his Lord dealt with the army that came with an elephant: he made their scheme go astray, sent flocks of birds against them that pelted them with stones of baked clay, and left them like chewed-up straw.
P6534: Everything in heaven and earth glorifies God, who owns their kingdom, gives life and death and can do all things. He is first and last, evident and hidden. He made heavens and earth in six days and took the throne; he knows what enters and leaves earth and sky, and is with people wherever they are.
P3978: When the earth is shaken violently and throws out its burdens, man will ask what is wrong with it. That day it will tell its news, because its Lord has inspired it. People will come out in scattered groups to be shown their deeds: whoever did an atom's weight of good will see it, and likewise of evil.
P9063: This scripture was sent so the listener may bring people from darkness into light, onto the path of God, owner of everything. Woe to deniers who prefer this life to the next, block God's way and seek to bend it. Every messenger spoke his own people's language to make things clear; God guides or misleads as he wills.
P2273: By the panting chargers that strike sparks, raid at dawn, raise dust and plunge into the enemy's midst: man is ungrateful to his Lord, witnesses this himself, and loves wealth fiercely. Does he not know that when graves are emptied and the secrets of hearts brought out, their Lord will know all about them that day?
P4061: The Merciful taught the recitation, created man and taught him speech. Sun and moon follow a reckoning; plants and trees bow. He raised the sky and set the balance: weigh justly, do not cheat. He spread the earth for creatures: fruit, sheathed palms, husked grain and herbs. Which favors will the two addressed deny? Man came from potter's clay.
P1234: By the sky and the piercing night star, every soul has a watcher. Man was made from gushing fluid issuing between backbone and ribs; God can restore him on the day secrets are tested and he stands helpless. By the returning sky and splitting earth, this is decisive speech, not jest. They plot, God plots; grant deniers brief respite.
P5512: When the inevitable event comes, undeniable, lowering some and raising others, the earth will be shaken and the mountains crumbled to scattered dust. People will be three groups: those of the right, those of the left, and the foremost, brought near in gardens of delight, many from earlier generations and few from later, reclining face to face on woven couches.
P1188: Believers must keep agreements. Livestock is lawful with stated exceptions, but hunting is forbidden in the pilgrim state. They must not violate God's rites, the sacred month, the offerings and garlanded animals, or those travelling to the sacred house. Hatred of people who barred them from the sanctuary must not lead to aggression; cooperate in goodness, not sin.
P7826: The listener is reminded that his chest was opened, the burden that weighed down his back was lifted, and his reputation raised. He is told twice that ease comes with hardship. So when he is free he should keep striving and direct his longing to his Lord.
P4538: Glorify the Lord most high, who creates and shapes, determines and guides, and turns green pasture to dark stubble. The listener will recite without forgetting, unless God wills, his path made easy. He should remind: the fearful heed, the wretch turns away and enters the great fire, neither dying nor living. Whoever purifies himself and prays succeeds.
P4996: By the clear scripture, recited in a named language to be understood, and exalted in the source record with God. Should the reminder be withheld because people are excessive? Many earlier prophets were mocked, and stronger peoples destroyed. Asked who created heavens and earth, they would name the mighty, knowing one, who made the earth a cradle with roads.
P3017: God has heard the woman who argued about her husband and complained to him. Men who declare their wives to be like their mothers speak falsely; only those who bore them are mothers. If they retract, they must free a slave before touching their wives, or fast two consecutive months, or feed sixty poor people. These are God's limits.
P8000: When God's help and victory arrive and the listener sees people entering God's religion in crowds, he should glorify his Lord with praise and ask his forgiveness, for he is always ready to accept repentance.
P6889: By the fig and the olive, by a mountain and by this secure city: man was created in the finest form, then brought down to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do good, whose reward never ends. What then can make anyone deny the judgment? Is God not the wisest of judges?
P2511: Praise to God who made heavens and earth, darkness and light; yet deniers set up equals to him. He made people from clay and fixed a term known to him, yet they doubt. He knows what they hide, show and earn. They turn from every sign and denied the truth; news of what they mocked will reach them.
P1905: A man is cursed: may his hands perish, and he is ruined. His wealth and his earnings will not help him. He will burn in a flaming fire, and so will his wife, the carrier of firewood, with a rope of twisted fiber around her neck.
P7818: This scripture is undoubtedly from the Lord of the worlds; not invented but truth, to warn a people never warned before. God created heavens, earth and all between in six days, then took the throne; no other protector or intercessor exists. He directs affairs from heaven to earth; they rise to him in a day like a thousand years.
P7175: By time, humankind is in a state of loss, except for those who believe, do good deeds, and urge one another to truth and to patience.
P7968: An oath by the day of rising and the self-reproaching soul. Man thinks his bones will not be gathered; God can restore even his fingertips. Yet he wants to keep sinning and asks when that day is. When sight is dazzled, the moon darkened and joined with the sun, he finds no refuge and is told all he did.
P6863: The listener has been given abundance, so he should pray to his Lord and offer sacrifice. It is the one who hates him who will be cut off.
P8929: A scripture is sent to the listener, who should feel no unease about it, to warn and remind. People should follow it and no other patrons. Many towns were destroyed at night or midday rest, crying only that they had done wrong. Messengers and their audiences will be questioned; deeds will be weighed, and heavy scales bring success.
P3930: People must fear their Lord who made them from one soul, made its mate from it and spread many men and women from them, and must respect kinship. Orphans' property must be given, not swapped for worse or consumed. If one fears wronging orphans, marry two, three or four women; if unfairness is feared, only one, or a bondwoman.
P5784: By covering night, bright day and the making of male and female, people's efforts differ. Whoever gives, is mindful and affirms goodness is eased toward ease; the self-satisfied miser who denies it is eased toward hardship, his wealth useless when he falls. Fire awaits the denying wretch; spared is the devout who gives to purify himself, owing no one repayment.
P4884: A true story of a prophet and a tyrant who divided his people and oppressed one group, killing sons and sparing women. God meant to make the oppressed leaders and heirs and show the tyrant what he feared. The prophet's mother was inspired to nurse him and, if afraid, cast him into the river; he would return a messenger.
P8679: One wrapped in a cloak is told to rise and warn, magnify his Lord, cleanse his garments, shun defilement, give without seeking gain, and be patient. The trumpet blast brings a hard day for deniers. Leave to God a man given wealth and sons who greedily wants more and stubbornly opposed the signs; a steep climb awaits him.
P6657: By sun and moon, day and night, sky and earth, and the soul shown its wickedness and piety: whoever purifies it succeeds, whoever buries it fails. A people denied in arrogance; their worst man rose, and despite the messenger's warning about God's she-camel and her drink, they hamstrung her, so their Lord crushed and levelled them, fearing no consequence.
P4779: This scripture comes from God, who created heavens and earth in truth and for a fixed term, though deniers ignore the warning. They are challenged to show what their other deities created on earth or share in the heavens, or produce an earlier scripture or trace of knowledge. None strays further than one calling on those who never answer.
P5342: By the setting star, their companion neither strays nor speaks from whim: it is revelation, taught by a mighty one who stood on the highest horizon, drew within two bow-lengths and revealed. His heart did not falsify what he saw. He saw him again by the farthest boundary tree, near the garden of refuge, when something enveloped the tree.
P5915: The prophet is told that divorce must observe the waiting period, counted carefully. Wives are not to be expelled from their homes, nor leave, unless guilty of open indecency; God may bring a change afterward. When the term ends, keep them or part from them honorably, before two just witnesses. Whoever is mindful of God is given a way out.
P5424: By the sky of constellations, the promised day, witness and witnessed: doomed are the makers of the fuel-fed fire pit, who sat watching what they did to believers, hated only for believing in God, who witnesses everything. Those who torment believing men and women without repenting face burning; believers who do good get gardens with flowing rivers, the great triumph.
P4832: By the wise recitation, the listener is a messenger on a straight path, sent to warn a heedless people whose fathers went unwarned. Most will not believe: their necks are shackled to the chin, and barriers before and behind blind them. Warning helps only one who follows the reminder and fears the Merciful unseen; promise him forgiveness and reward.
P1825: These verses of a wise scripture are guidance and mercy for those who do good, pray, give alms and are certain of the hereafter. But someone buys idle tales to mislead from God's path and mock it, and haughtily turns from the verses as if deaf; he faces humiliating, painful punishment. Believers who do good have gardens of delight.
P6207: A scripture of verses perfected then detailed from one wise and aware: worship only God. The speaker warns and brings good news; seek forgiveness and repent to enjoy good provision for a term, or fear a great day. All return to God. Some fold their chests to hide from him, but even under their garments he knows their secrets.
P6019: Glory to him who took his servant by night from the sacred place of worship to the farthest one, with blessed surroundings, to show him signs. A prophet was given a scripture guiding a people to trust God alone. They were warned they would twice spread corruption and arrogance; the first time, mighty servants of God ravaged their homes.
P6418: A command to say that God is one, the eternal one on whom all depend; he has not fathered anyone nor was he born, and nothing is equal or comparable to him.
P2450: One wrapped up is told to stand in prayer most of the night, about half, slightly less or more, reciting slowly, for a weighty word is coming. Night rising is more intense and speech then truer; the day is busy. He should remember his Lord devotedly, trust the lord of east and west, bear people's talk and withdraw graciously.
P3534: Hypocrites come testifying that the listener is God's messenger; God knows he is, and testifies that they lie. They shield themselves with oaths and block God's way; having believed then denied, their hearts are sealed. Their looks impress and their speech attracts, yet they are like propped-up timber, thinking every cry targets them. They are the enemy; beware.
P8911: Praise God, owner of all in heaven and earth, praised also in the hereafter. He knows what enters and leaves the earth, what descends from and ascends to the sky. Deniers say the hour will not come; swear that it will. Not an atom's weight, smaller or larger, escapes his clear record, so believers who do good are rewarded.
P1369: By those that pull out forcefully, draw out gently, glide, race ahead and manage affairs: on the day of the quake and its aftershock, hearts pound and eyes drop. People ask if rotten bones can be restored; one shout and they are on the surface. Then: a prophet was called in a sacred valley and sent to a transgressing tyrant.
P6496: Has news come of the overwhelming event? Some faces are downcast, toiling and exhausted, entering scorching fire, drinking from a boiling spring, fed only bitter thorns that neither nourish nor satisfy. Others are radiant, pleased with their striving, in a high garden without idle talk, a flowing spring, raised couches, cups, cushions and carpets. Consider how camels were made.
P2537: People ask one another about the great news they dispute; they will soon know. Did God not make the earth a bed, mountains pegs, people in pairs, sleep for rest, night a cover, day for livelihood, seven strong heavens above, a blazing lamp, and pouring rain bringing grain, plants and dense gardens? The day of decision is fixed.
P3298: Blessed is the one who holds all dominion and power, who created death and life to test who acts best, and seven layered heavens without flaw. Look again and again for cracks: the gaze returns defeated and weary. The lowest heaven is adorned with lamps, made missiles against devils, for whom blazing punishment is prepared.
